Resolves #21361

The web desktop's launcher now lays its icons out the way a desktop does: one column per group from the top left, each under a sentence-case caption, with no full-width rule. A group taller than the launcher continues in the next column, and a phone keeps rows. The drag takes SortZone's vertical halves, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Up/Down move an app as Left/Right do. CSS Grid's own auto-placement does the grouping, because a caption placed at row 1 opens a new column. `list.Base`'s flat items stay as they are.

Evidence: L3 (unit arms red on `dev` and green here; live Chromium frames of the head and of `dev` at the same viewports) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-3 frames, AC-4 unit arms, AC-5 cold read). Residual: none.

## Cold look

Three readers without context ran one at a time. Each saw one frame and answered the same three questions: what is this screen, how much does it look like a finished product a visitor would trust (1 to 10), and what is its weakest point.

| Frame | What it is, in their words | Grade | Weakest point |
|---|---|---|---|
| after, neo-dark | "a web desktop or launcher screen" | 6 | the icons sit top left, and about 60% of the screen is empty |
| after, neo-light | "a desktop-style app launcher or 'home screen'" | 6 | the icons are crammed top left, about 80% of the screen is empty, and there is no title or branding |
| before, neo-dark (control) | "an app launcher or desktop-style home screen" | 5 | "the section divider lines stretch across the page but hold only two or three small icons each" |

The rules left the weakest-point list, and the grade went from 5 to 6. The control also shows that AC-5's "neither calls it a settings page" does not discriminate on its own: the before reader did not say "settings page" either. All three readers named the same remaining gap, unprompted. The icons cluster top left, and nothing on the screen says what the product is. That gap goes to #21198 as the next design step; it is not this ticket's.

## Deltas from ticket

- A label truncates with an ellipsis instead of overflowing its tile, because a tile now has a fixed 96px slot.
- The key handlers are `onKeyDownNext` and `onKeyDownPrevious` now, since Left and Right are no longer the only keys bound to them.
- From review: the main thread's navigator also took Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down as plain arrows and moved the focus. `Neo.main.addon.Navigator#subscribe` gains `workerChords`, beside `workerKeys`: arrow, Home and End pressed with Ctrl or Cmd belong to the App Worker. It is off by default, and the launcher declares it.

## Test Evidence

- Red-first: in a base worktree at `289d1a2db3` with this spec copied in, exactly the two changed arms fail (the drop axis, and Down/Up). All 15 pass at the head.
- Frames: Playwright against the dev server. For the before frames, `dev`'s built launcher CSS stood in for the head's in the untracked `dist/`. The after frames are rebuilt from the head.
- Geometry at 1440 × 900: every tile is 96px tall, exactly its four 24px rows, every caption is 19px, and no label truncates.
